findings.title: Negative offset bypasses pagination validation
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result allows attacker-controlled Cursor.offset < 0 to be passed directly to Django queryset slicing as queryset[start_offset:stop] when enable_advanced_features is true. Django does not support negative slicing and other paginators explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError. The comment that Django handles it automatically is false. Consequence is unhandled AssertionError/500 denial of service and bypass of established pagination bounds checking.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate datetime keys
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value as int. When used from organization_auditlogs.py with order_by='-datetime' the key value is a datetime object, not a number, so math.floor raises TypeError and the cursor value (int) compared against a datetime column in build_queryset produces wrong SQL or DB error. Consequence is the optimized audit-log path is broken and crashes instead of paginating.

findings.title: Query-param-gated switch to vulnerable paginator
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py a request with ?optimized_pagination=true plus is_superuser or has_global_access switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. This exposes the negative-offset path and numeric-only cursor logic to any user satisfying that weak gate on a sensitive audit-log endpoint. Consequence is expanded attack surface for DoS and incorrect access to audit data beyond normal pagination.

findings.title: Inconsistent negative-offset handling in BasePaginator
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors with max(0, offset) but passes offset unchanged for is_prev cursors to queryset[offset:stop]. A crafted prev cursor with negative offset therefore still reaches Django queryset slicing which rejects negative indexing, causing 500, while forward cursors silently rewrite invalid input to 0 hiding client bugs. Both cases should raise BadPaginationError like other paginators. Consequence is inconsistent errors and silent correction of invalid cursors.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE without aggregate corrupts scores on duplicates
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua merging uses redis.call('zunionstore', set_key, 2, set_key, span_key) with default AGGREGATE SUM. Members are span payloads with score end_timestamp_precise. If the same payload already exists in both sets, for example on retry or duplicate ingest, the score is summed and doubled instead of preserved. Consequence is inflated timestamps, wrong zpopmin eviction order and wrong segment ordering.

findings.title: Oversized-segment guard removed, silent truncation without observability
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/buffer.py _load_segment_data no longer enforces max_segment_spans and the constructor field max_segment_spans is now dead. The Lua script truncates sets to 1000 with zpopmin without emitting metrics.incr or logging, unlike the previous path that dropped too-large segments with segment_span_count_exceeded and an error log. Consequence is silent data loss where oldest spans including a potential root span can be evicted with no alerting and operators cannot tune via max_segment_spans.

findings.title: Direct required-field access crashes consumer on bad message
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch does val['end_timestamp_precise'] with direct indexing. Any message missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo processing step, stalling or crash-looping the spans consumer on a poison message instead of skipping or defaulting. Consequence is availability risk for the whole partition on malformed input.
